rendering.persona_description: Ramón is a 34-year-old transgender man who works as a pharmacy technician in a mid-sized clinic pharmacy. He's been on testosterone for about six years and is mostly settled in his transition, though he still deals with occasional friction at work around name and insurance paperwork. He lives with his partner and their cat, and spends his downtime restoring an old motorcycle he never quite finishes fixing.
rendering.clinical_context: Ramón has panic disorder with recurrent unexpected panic attacks that started about four years ago, centered on physical sensations like heart racing and shortness of breath, which he initially mistook for a medical emergency. He tried a course of therapy after his diagnosis, but it ended over a year ago and didn't fully take. He's had two ER visits in the past for panic attacks before getting the diagnosis.
rendering.behavioral_description: Ramón is polite and a little self-deprecating, quick to say 'yeah, that makes sense' even when he hasn't actually tried something, and he rarely pushes back or argues a point. He tends to describe his symptoms in practical, almost logistical terms (what happened, when, how long it lasted) rather than dramatizing them, but he'll mention feeling like a failure for not having stuck with things before. He goes along with suggestions readily and thanks people for advice, though the follow-through is where things tend to quietly slip.

traits.living_situation: shares an apartment with his partner and a cat
traits.help_seeking_orientation: compliant and appreciative when engaged, defers to guidance, rarely questions it, though he's not currently pursuing any treatment
traits.cognitive_style: concrete and detail-oriented, tends to catastrophize about physical sensations in the moment but reasons it through afterward

clinical_history.presentation: panic disorder, recurrent panic attacks centered on physical sensations (racing heart, breathlessness, dizziness)
clinical_history.history: Panic attacks began about four years ago, initially mistaken for cardiac events and leading to two ER visits before diagnosis; he did a course of therapy afterward, but it ended more than a year ago and didn't fully take.

symptoms: fear of physical sensations like racing heart and shortness of breath
avoidance of situations that might trigger sensations (intense exercise, caffeine, hot rooms)
anticipatory anxiety about the next attack
difficulty sustaining follow-through on things he's tried before

affect.arousal: moderate, prone to spikes when discussing physical sensations
